patches.rationale: Business annual policies commonly allow customers to choose a per‑trip maximum duration (e.g., 30/60/90 days). Capturing discrete options improves comparability versus a single max value.
patches.description: Selectable per‑trip maximum duration options (days) for Annual Multi‑Trip policies. Represent each option as objects: {value_days, notes}.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Who should take this policy? … gives You the choice of 30, 60 or 90 days for the maximum duration of any one trip. (p2)

patches.rationale: Cover‑More Business explicitly includes leisure travel weeks within the annual policy. This is a frequent differentiator for business policies and useful for comparisons.
patches.description: Weeks of leisure/personal travel included within the Business annual policy year, if offered.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: The policy … includes up to 6 weeks of leisure travel during the year. (p2)

patches.rationale: Business plans often include an ‘Alternative staff’ benefit. Adding this alias will help normalise mapping to the existing business_benefits category.
patches.description: Add alias to capture ‘Alternative staff’ under business‑specific benefits.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Benefits table: 9 Alternative staff – $15,000. (pp4–5)

patches.rationale: Business travel policies are inherently annual multi‑trip. Extend applies_to so the classifier can be emitted for business products.
patches.description: Trip frequency classification as marketed.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: The business policy offers annual cover designed for business travellers who go away multiple times during the year. (p2)

patches.rationale: Business annual multi‑trip plans have a selectable per‑trip duration; retaining the existing max field but extending scope to business enables recording the chosen cap when only a single selected value is available.
patches.description: Maximum journey duration allowed per trip for Annual Multi‑Trip (days).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: …choice of 30, 60 or 90 days for the maximum duration of any one trip. (p2)

patches.rationale: Business products also require selecting areas/regions of travel; extend scope accordingly.
patches.description: Geographic scope/areas of travel selection options as described (e.g., Worldwide, All of Europe, All of Asia, Australia).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Policy inclusions and options – Areas of travel. Guidance on selecting countries/regions; Worldwide option. (p5)

patches.rationale: Business plan has Amendment or cancellation costs with specified limits; enabling capture aligns comparisons.
patches.description: Cancellation cover amount. For products where the customer chooses an amount, store 'selected_amount' with any min/max/steps; otherwise store the fixed/maximum limit.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Benefits table: Amendment or cancellation costs – $Unlimited (sub‑limits apply). (pp4–5)

patches.rationale: Business cover includes overseas medical; extend applies_to so headline medical limit can be captured for business plans.
patches.description: Overseas medical cover headline limit (e.g., Unlimited). Include time caps if stated (e.g., up to 12 months from onset).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Overseas medical expenses – $Unlimited (cover will not exceed 12 months from onset). (p4)

patches.rationale: Emergency dental limits are specified in the business plan; enable capture for business type.
patches.description: Emergency dental limit per person.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Overseas dental expenses – $2,000. (p4)

patches.rationale: Business plan defines a baggage/personal effects overall limit; extend scope to business.
patches.description: Baggage/personal effects overall limit per person.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Luggage and travel documents – $25,000. (p4)

patches.rationale: Per‑item limits (e.g., phone, laptop, camera) are provided for the business plan; extend to capture sub‑limits for business type.
patches.description: Baggage common sub-limits (e.g., phones, cameras, laptops, jewellery). Represent as objects: {item_category, per_item_limit_aud, aggregate_cap_aud_if_any}.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Luggage item limits table (e.g., Phone $2,500; Camera/Video camera $6,000; Laptop $5,000; Tablet $3,000; Jewellery/Watch $1,500). (p6)

patches.rationale: Business plan supports specifying items/raising limits with valuation rules; extend scope so these rules are captured for business.
patches.description: Whether customers can increase item limits or specify items and the total/ per-item caps for specified items.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Increase luggage item limits by specifying items; receipt/valuation <2 years; up to $4,500 per item and overall increase up to $15,000. (pp6, 26)

patches.rationale: Business plan includes a defined Rental Car insurance excess limit; include business in scope.
patches.description: Rental vehicle insurance excess benefit limit per person.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Rental Car insurance excess – $10,000. (p4); Section 7 confirms $10,000. (p27)

patches.rationale: Business plan states a personal liability limit; extend scope accordingly.
patches.description: Personal liability maximum cover per person.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Personal liability – $5,000,000. (p4)

patches.rationale: Business plan provides Loss of income, Disability and Accidental death amounts and waiting periods; extend scope to business to normalise capture.
patches.description: Personal accident benefits: include components such as loss_of_income (weekly cap, max weeks), total_permanent_disablement, accidental_death. Represent as objects with fields {component, amount_aud, per_week_aud_if_applicable, max_weeks, age_applicability}.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Loss of income – up to $45,000 (max liability collectively for Sections 14–16 $45,000); Disability $30,000; Accidental death $30,000. (p4) Waiting period 15 days applies. (p29)

patches.rationale: COVID‑19 benefits are explicitly defined for the business plan (medical, additional expenses, cancellation sub‑limits); include business so summary can be captured consistently.
patches.description: COVID-19 coverage summary: which sections are covered (medical, cancellation before/after departure, additional expenses), notable sub-limits and compulsory special excesses.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: SECTION 18: COVID‑19 benefits – coverage for medical ($Unlimited), Additional expenses (with conditions), and Amendment or cancellation costs up to $10,000 per policy; exclusions noted. (pp31–32)

patches.rationale: Business plan defines waiting periods (e.g., loss of income). Extend scope so such deferrals can be recorded for business products.
patches.description: Key waiting periods or deferrals (e.g., loss of income waiting days; already travelling 3-day no-cover period if applicable).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Section 14 Loss of income – ‘not in respect of the first 15 days after You originally planned to resume Your work’. (p29)

patches.rationale: Business plan offers optional cover (e.g., motorcycle/moped, snow sports). Extend scope so add‑ons can be captured for business products.
patches.description: Optional add-ons available for the plan (e.g., cruise cover, skiing/snowboarding, motorcycle/moped, adventure activities packs, business pack, cancellation plus, specified items).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Motorcycle/moped riding – ‘If You wish to be covered … You must pay an extra premium.’ (p7) Snow skiing/snowboarding/snowmobiling – ‘… must pay an extra premium.’ (p7)

patches.rationale: Business plan specifies 24/7 assistance and thresholds; include business so these can be recorded.
patches.description: 24/7 emergency assistance contact details and any triage/approval thresholds (e.g., call if admitted, surgery, or costs over $2,000).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: 24 hour emergency assistance … You, or someone on Your behalf, should phone … if Your medical expenses will exceed $2,000 or if You want to return early. (p14)

patches.rationale: Claims evidence/notification rules are defined for the business plan; extend scope so they can be captured for business products.
patches.description: Claim reporting requirements (e.g., report theft to police within 7 days, PIR required, provide receipts, lodge within 60 days).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Claims – online or form; need receipts/support. Report theft/loss within 7 days to police/transport/accommodation; PIR needed where applicable. (pp14, 26–27)
